root_cause: The shared orchestrator-api mission resolver funnels --mission selectors through resolve_handle_to_read_path, which correctly calls assert_safe_path_segment and raises ValueError for values containing '..'. The machine-facing resolver adapter only translated resolver-specific not-found/fail-closed errors into JSON envelopes, so the safe-path ValueError escaped Typer/Click command execution and surfaced as a raw Python traceback instead of the orchestrator-api error envelope.
approach: Handle unsafe selector ValueError at the existing shared _resolve_mission_dir_or_fail seam so every orchestrator-api subcommand that accepts --mission gets the same JSON-first behavior. Map the exception to an INVALID_MISSION envelope with the original diagnostic in data.message, preserving existing StatusReadPathNotFound and MISSION_NOT_FOUND handling. Add a root-CLI regression test that invokes mission-state, list-ready, and resolve-workspace with '..' selectors and asserts non-zero parseable JSON with no traceback.
tests_to_add: Parameterized root CLI regression covering orchestrator-api mission-state --mission ../traversal
Parameterized root CLI regression covering orchestrator-api mission-state --mission ..
Parameterized root CLI regression covering orchestrator-api list-ready --mission ../traversal
Parameterized root CLI regression covering orchestrator-api resolve-workspace --mission .. --wp WP01
risk_notes: Catching broad ValueError at the resolver adapter could accidentally classify unrelated resolver ValueErrors as INVALID_MISSION; keep the catch tightly scoped around mission resolution and preserve the message for diagnosis.
out_of_scope_observations: The related human-facing next/research traceback from issue #2878 is a separate CLI surface and should not be changed in this fix.
